source_quality.boundary: Author claims, the official task, formula crops and the printed figures are kept separate. All 25 pages reviewed. Exact images only through bounded proxies.
source_quality.not_reproduced: The forecast, the dynamic program, the genetic search and the reported terminal values are source statements only.

task_reconstruction.source: 2022 MCM Problem C, as restated by the authors on page 3. Only what the paper states is recorded.
official_tasks: Give an optimal strategy and the value of the 1000 dollars on 9/10/2021.
Prove the strategy is optimal in different situations.
Show how trading costs change the strategy and the result.
Write a letter to traders summarizing the strategy, the model and the results.
task_reconstruction.data_boundary: Daily gold and bitcoin prices. The paper runs 9/10/2016 to 9/10/2021 and names no source file. The market-day rule and the commission rates are not stated in the restatement. Table 7 implies 1 percent on gold and 2 percent on bitcoin.

contributions.summary: The combined ARIMA-LSTM forecast is accurate enough to base trades on.; The trading strategy uses the ARIMA-LSTM predictions.
Dynamic programming turns the five-year problem into daily decisions.; The baseline strategy and its terminal value.
Encoding the strategy as four genes and selecting on yield improves it.; The reported strategy is the genetically optimized one, with the higher terminal value.
The strategy is optimal because it still wins when the strategy or the market changes.; The optimality claim in the summary and the memorandum.
Changing transaction costs changes trading frequency and return together.; The sensitivity statement reported to the investor.

steps: select by roulette wheel and backtesting
algorithm.convergence_criteria: The paper says the process repeats until the results converge to the optimal solution, and gives no numeric tolerance.

strengths: The encoding separates the strategy into four choices the search can vary one at a time.
limitations: With yield as the only fitness, the search ignores risk, which the weakness section later concedes.
missing_details: No population size, crossover probability, or mutation probability is given.

verification.summary: Table 1 puts the combined RMSE at 0.0342 and MAPE at 0.36, against 0.7034 and 7.21 for ARIMA and 0.6183 and 6.25 for LSTM.
Changing the selling gene is offered as one half of the optimality argument. The page prints the yield falling from 442 percent.
The bull, bear and oscillating charts are the other half. All three are numbered Figure 16.
The commission table has four rows. The figure caption says five costs, and the legend cannot be read.

results_trace.summary: The summary discounts the dynamic-programming result to $360,595.32 and prints a return of 37456.33 percent.
Page 11 prints $374,563.25 on 9/10/21, worth $360,595.32 on 9/10/16, and a total return written as is3745.63 percent.
Page 15 prints $442,697.25, a five-year return of 44,169.70 percent, and an annualized return of 338.08 percent.
The memorandum prints a 440x return and signs the letter Lee, dated February 21, 2022.

language_observations.summary: Narrow the cause of profit from the asset to the strategy, which the paper can actually control. / stakes-then-contrast
Announce the two models as a colon list, each with a label and a job. / model-announcement
Set two methods as mirrors, one taking the linear part and the other the non-linear part. / method-contrast-mirror
Put the two error numbers directly after the qualitative claim so the adjective is not left bare. / number-replaces-adjective
Give the dollar result, then the discounted dollar, then a 'which means' clause that ties each dollar to its date. / result-then-discount
Announce the number of proofs and name each, then treat them in that same order. / announce-then-follow
Close the summary by pointing at the letter and listing its contents with a run of participles. / closing-pointer
Announce a count, name the items with 'namely', then say what the list is for. / counted-namely-list
Turn a fact about the world into the research question with a single 'so'. / scene-so-question
Concede the obvious objection in a blunt colloquial sentence before building on it. / concession-opening
Use 'However' to bring in the second asset as the remedy for the first asset's flaw. / however-as-remedy
Set up a proverb-like example and cash it out with 'Therefore' into this paper's decision. / proverb-then-therefore
Credit the problem statement, then announce the task list that the rest of the paper answers. / task-routing
Hand the work plan to a figure in one sentence instead of narrating it. / plan-handed-to-figure
State each assumption and follow it at once with a justification, four times. / assumption-justification-pair
Define a term with a colon, a one-line definition, then one sentence of character. / term-colon-definition
Point to the notation table in one sentence instead of glossing every symbol in prose. / notation-table-pointer
Move from a known series to the unknown future price and then point to the equation. / known-to-future-then-equation
Justify combining two methods by the mixed nature of the market, using 'so'. / combine-by-necessity
Gloss every symbol in an equation with a 'Where' sentence, one clause each. / where-symbol-gloss
Read a figure as a count of steps, then give each step as 'Step N: action'. / figure-to-steps
Describe dynamic programming as splitting one long problem into daily pieces. / split-long-into-short
Read a figure as a weakness first, then concede with 'However' what it still does. / figure-reading-with-concession
Draw a conclusion from a figure with 'Therefore, we can conclude', and keep it qualified. / therefore-we-conclude
Narrate a multi-stage method with firstly through finally, one stage per ordinal. / ordinal-stages
Read a table with 'it is not difficult to find', state the result, then give the reason with 'because'. / table-reading-then-reason
Hand the result of one section to the next section with 'Therefore, in the part of'. / section-handoff
State the result, then compare it against the two assets over the same period. / result-against-benchmark
Introduce each gene as a name, a role, and a pointer to its encoding table. / gene-name-role-table
Decode one code as an example, then claim the table is exhaustive. / example-then-exhaustive
Concede that many measures exist, then justify the single one by what the data allows. / although-only-since
Explain an empty cell instead of leaving it to be read as a missing result. / empty-cell-explanation
Restate the two-part proof and assign one change to each part. / two-part-proof
Read a regime chart as what the strategy did, in plain 'as you can see'. / chart-as-you-can-see
Compare the two returns and close with 'so it can be justified'. / comparison-so-justified
Motivate the sensitivity test by the gap between an ideal result and a costly one. / ideal-but-costly
Introduce a scenario table with 'to see the impact, we replaced X with the following N scenarios'. / scenario-table-intro
Report a sensitivity result as 'we find that when X, Y'. / we-find-that-when
Open the letter in the first person singular, then shift to we. / letter-opening-shift
Flag a risk with 'it is worth noting' before the caveat. / worth-noting-caveat
Close the letter with thanks and a wish, not with a result. / letter-closing-wish
State a strength as a by-doing clause that names the benefit. / strength-by-doing
State a weakness as only-uses, without-considering, so the limit. / weakness-only-without-so
Open the conclusion by rejecting an all-knowing stance, and close it with 'in short' plus a verdict. / conclusion-frame

weaknesses.summary: The prose defines d as the number of differences when the series is stationary, which reverses the usual meaning, and equation (2) does not contain d. The skill may teach an ARIMA with an explicit difference order. It must not copy this definition or treat equation (2) as using d.

Equation (4) in the figure, recorded as EQ-004, multiplies by i_t and by a tilde-C, and neither symbol has a printed equation. The skill may say the paper names both in prose. It must not supply the missing gate equations.
Equation (1) uses Y_T and equation (2) uses y_t. The paper never identifies them. The skill may keep both symbols. It must not write y_t = Y_T.
Equation (3) divides by (1 + r_f)^n. The Where gloss never defines n, and the page never prints r_f. The skill may report the two dollar figures as printed. It must not check or rebuild the discount.

The left side is spelled Yeild, and the right side is a single selling price over a single buying price. The page then calls the result the total return, is3745.63%. The skill may quote the spelling and the per-trade ratio. It must not teach that ratio as the account return.

The summary prints 37456.33%. Page 11 prints is3745.63% beside the terminal value $374,563.25 and the discounted $360,595.32. Neither percent equals the dollar ratio. The skill may quote each figure with its page. It must not pick one as the return.

The summary prints 44269.73% and an annualized 338.08%. Page 15 prints $442,697.25, 44,169.70%, bitcoin 7458.97%, gold 135.48%, and the same 338.08%. The memorandum prints a 440x return. Pages 17-18 print that the changed yield was reduced from 442% is reduced to 273%. The skill may keep the dollar terminal. It must not treat these percents as one number.

Table 6 prints 259.05% on 2018-1-15 and 3.718426 on 2021-4-21. Early bitcoin cells have a percent sign and later ones do not. Gold cells are decimals. The skill may teach the empty-cell sentence. It must not merge the prose percents with the cells.
Section 6.3.1 cites Tables 2 and 3. Those tables are the Gene1 and Gene2 encodings. The returns are in Table 6. The skill must not follow the citation.
Figure 10 draws one cyan line and no legend. No observed series is on the chart. The skill may say the prose claims accuracy. It must not say the figure shows the match.
Both charts label the vertical axis Cases and mark it times 10 to the 4. The skill may describe the two lines. It must not read Cases as the unit or as a dollar price.

Both captions end on 2021/9/10. Both x-axes print 2023/3/15, and point labels collide with the dates. The skill may use the caption interval and the terminal labels 374563.25 and 442697.25. It must not date the overlapping labels.
Table 7 has four commission rows and no baseline. Figure 17 draws five curves, and the legend text is too small to read. The skill may say costs were varied. It must not assign a curve to a row.

Table 1 is the notation table and the performance table. Figure 13 is the genetic-algorithm flow and the bitcoin trade chart. Figure 16 is the bull, bear, and oscillating charts. Table 6 is the return table and the stop-loss table. The skill must cite the caption, not the number alone.

The same three-bit codes are reused across Gene1, Gene2, Gene3, and Gene4, and 100 is printed before 011. In the stop-loss table, 100 is also a dollar amount. The skill may copy one table at a time. It must not treat a code as stable across genes.
